components.note: Simplified from 寫; the modern shape is a shorthand with no readable picture

example.hanzi: 请把你的名字写在这里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de míngzi xiě zài zhèlǐ.
example.fact: 写 covers writing characters (写字), composing (写文章 'write an essay') and describing. It differs from 画 'draw'. Its traditional form 寫 is much more complex.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — something bored through, the original sense of 穿
牙 (yá) is a loose sound hint; teeth that bite through also fit the image

example.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
example.english: It's cold today, so wear more clothes.
example.fact: 穿 is used for clothes, shoes and socks, but hats, glasses and jewellery take 戴. Its original meaning is 'to pierce', which remains in 穿过 'pass through' and 看穿 'see through'.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — a precious object to hold and play with
廾 (two hands) — hands holding it, which is the old sense 'to play with'

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī nòng huài le.
example.fact: 弄 is a colloquial all-purpose verb that stresses the outcome: 弄坏 'break', 弄丢 'lose', 弄清楚 'make clear'. Read lòng it means 'alley', as in the Shanghai-style 弄堂.

meanings: particle: 了 + 啊, lively statement

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken particle
拉 (lā) gives the sound exactly

example.fact: 啦 is a fusion of 了 and 啊 and gives a bright, informal tone: 好啦 'OK, OK', 吃饭啦 'dinner's ready!'. It appears in speech and chat, and is rare in formal writing.

components.note: 去 (qù) gives a near sound for què
卩 (kneeling person) — an older meaning of 却 is 'retreat', related to this figure

example.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, què bù xiǎng xiūxi.
example.english: He is tired, but he doesn't want to rest.
example.fact: 却 goes after the subject and before the verb: 我想去，他却不想. It signals unexpected contrast and is often paired with 但是 or 可是: 他很聪明，但是却不努力. Unlike 但, it never starts a clause.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — counting rods were cut from bamboo
具 (tool) — a counting tool, together suggesting calculation

example.pinyin: Qǐng suàn yíxià zǒnggòng duōshao qián.
example.english: Please work out how much it is in total.
example.fact: 算 means 'to calculate', and by extension 'to count as': 这也算好吃 'this counts as tasty'. 算了 'forget it' and 打算 'plan to' are very common, as is 算数 'to count (as valid)'.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement
关 (guān) — the upper part; its reduced shape is best learned as a memory aid

example.fact: 送 covers gifts (送礼物), deliveries (送货) and escorting: 送你回家 'see you home', 送行 'see someone off'. 送给 marks the recipient: 送给她一朵花.

meanings: (in 以前, 以后) before, after

components.note: The origin is debated; learn it as a unit

example.fact: 以 is a formal 'by/using' that survives in set words: 可以 'may', 所以 'therefore', 以前 'before', 以后 'after', 以为 'to assume'. In writing it forms 以…为… 'take… as…'.

components.note: 王 (jade, in compound form) — an object to play with
元 (yuán) is a close sound match for wán

example.english: The children are playing in the park.
example.fact: 玩 is 'play for fun', not sport (that's 打球) and not instruments (弹钢琴). 玩手机 'mess about on the phone', 好玩 'fun', 玩笑 'joke'. 玩儿 is the Beijing form.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — the right part; the origin of the character is debated, so learn the whole as a unit

example.fact: 成 means 'become' (成为) and 'succeed': 成功 'success', 成绩 'results/grades'. As a result ending it means 'turn into': 变成 'become'. Northern speech uses 成 as 'OK': 成！ 'Fine!'

meanings: measure word for long thin things

components.note: 木 (tree) — the lower part; a slim twig is the 'strip' in the origin of the measure word

example.fact: 条 counts long, thin or flexible things: 路, 河, 鱼, 裤子 'trousers', 狗 'dog', 蛇 'snake'. It also means 'article/clause': 条件 'condition', 条约 'treaty'. Simplified from 條.

components.note: 多 (many) — enough means having plenty
句 (jù) gives a loose sound hint for gòu

example.fact: 够 means 'enough': 不够 'not enough', 够了！ 'That's enough!' Before an adjective it adds 'quite' (够大) and in the sense 'to reach' it needs ability: 够不着 'can't reach'.

components.note: 足 (foot) — running uses the feet
包 (bāo) is a close sound hint for pǎo

example.fact: 跑 is 'run' (in classical Chinese 走 meant 'run'). 跑步 is 'jogging/running', 跑腿 'run errands'. It can also mean 'flee' or 'leak': 车跑了 'the car left'.

components.note: A crescent moon

example.fact: 月 is both 'moon' and 'month'. Months are simply numbers + 月: 一月 to 十二月, and 月份 means 'month' in the calendar sense. The same shape also appears in body-part characters (as a form of 肉 'flesh').

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun at dawn
十 (cross) — a mark just beneath the sun, as it rises at the horizon

example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de hěn zǎo.
example.english: You got up very early today.
example.fact: 早 stands alone as 'Good morning!' (早！) and builds 早上 'morning', 早饭 'breakfast'. It can mean 'long ago': 我早就知道了 'I knew it long ago'. Its opposite is 晚.

components.note: Simplified from 長, which pictured a person with long flowing hair, hence 'long'

example.fact: 长 is read cháng for 'long' but zhǎng for 'grow' or 'chief': 长大 'grow up', 校长 'school principal', 长辈 'elders'. So the same character covers both 'long' and 'elder' in one old picture of long-haired age.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; the oldest sense of 号 is 'to shout'
丂 (kǎo) is a loose sound hint

example.fact: 号 gives the day of the month in speech: 三号 'the 3rd' (written 日). It also means 'number' (号码, 房间号) and 'size' (大号 'large'). Read háo it means 'to wail'.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old spear shaft was wooden
仓 (cāng) is a close sound hint for qiāng

example.english: The police officer has a gun.
example.fact: 枪 originally meant 'spear' and now mostly means 'gun': 手枪 'pistol', 开枪 'fire a gun'. Its measure word is 把 or 支. In 红缨枪 it still means a spear.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an animal radical
句 (jù) is a loose sound hint for gǒu

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì tiáo gǒu.
example.english: We have a dog at home.
example.fact: 狗 takes the measure word 条 or 只: 一条狗, 一只小狗. It's one of the twelve zodiac animals (属狗 'born in the Year of the Dog'). The word appears in many idioms; some are insults, so 狗 isn't always friendly.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — talk
炎 (yán) is a loose sound hint for tán

example.fact: 谈 is a more serious 'talk' than 说: 谈工作 'discuss work', 谈判 'negotiate'. 谈恋爱 means 'to date, be in a romantic relationship'. 谈话 'a talk' can be a formal conversation.

components.note: Simplified from 頭, whose 頁 part meant 'head'; the modern shape is a shorthand

example.fact: 头 is 'head' and the suffix of nouns: 石头 'stone', 木头 'wood', 骨头 'bone'. It also means 'first/top': 头一次 'the first time'. 头发 is 'hair', and 一头牛 counts a head of cattle.

components.note: Simplified from 歲; the modern parts are a shorthand rather than a clear picture

example.english: My daughter is five years old.
example.fact: 岁 gives age: 三岁 'three years old'. Ask a child 你几岁了？ and an adult 你多大了？ Respectfully, an elder is asked 您多大年纪？ The word also appears in 岁月 'years, time'.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water as a sign of life
舌 (shé) is only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo yú hái huó zhe.
example.fact: 活 is 'alive' and 'to live': 生活 'life', 活动 'activity', 活泼 'lively'. In speech 活 can also mean 'work': 干活 'do work'. It is different from 住 'live in (a place)'.

components.note: The origin is debated; learn it as a unit

example.fact: 者 is a suffix for people: 作者 'author', 记者 'journalist', 读者 'reader', 学者 'scholar'. In classical Chinese it means 'the one who…'. It never stands alone in modern speech.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken call
畏 (wèi) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Wèi, qǐngwèn shì Wáng xiānsheng ma?
example.english: Hello, may I ask if this is Mr. Wang?
example.fact: 喂 is the standard phone 'hello', also read wéi by some speakers. It is also a verb, 'to feed': 喂孩子 'feed the child', 喂狗 'feed the dog'. Use it to call someone's attention, but it can sound blunt.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — complete, a roof covering everything
元 (yuán) is a close sound match for wán

example.fact: 完 is a common result ending: 吃完 'finish eating', 写完, 看完. Alone, 完了 means 'it's over' or 'oh no!'. 完全 means 'completely'.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — stretching a bowstring, the original sense of 'stretch, open'
长 (cháng/zhǎng) is a close sound hint for zhāng

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng piào.
example.fact: 张 counts flat things: 纸 'paper', 票 'tickets', 桌子 'tables', 床 'beds', 照片 'photos'. It is also the very common surname Zhāng, and 张开 means 'to open wide'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — a hand action
妾 (qiè) is a loose sound hint for jiē

example.english: I'll go to the airport to pick you up.
example.fact: 接 means 'pick up' (a person), 'answer' (接电话) and 'connect'. 接受 means 'accept' and 接着 'then, next'. Its opposite for people is 送 'see off'.

components.note: 土 (earth) — an open piece of ground
勿 (wù) is a shorthand that replaces the older sound part 昜 (yáng), so the clue is lost

example.pinyin: Zuótiān xià le yì chǎng dà yǔ.
example.english: There was a heavy rain yesterday.
example.fact: 场 counts events: 一场电影, 一场比赛, 一场大雨. It also names places: 机场 'airport', 市场 'market', 广场 'square'. Read cháng, it means 'threshing floor'.

components.note: An old form is said to show a fur garment, with 'seek' a borrowed sense; the fur sense is now written 裘

example.pinyin: Wǒ qiú nǐ bāng wǒ yí ge máng.
example.english: I beg you to do me a favour.
example.fact: 求 is stronger than 请: 求你了 'please, I'm begging you'. It forms 要求 'demand', 请求 'request', 求助 'seek help' and 求婚 'to propose marriage'. It also means 'seek': 追求 'pursue'.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — a hard blade, the old link with 'hard, firm'
冈 (gāng) gives the sound exactly

example.fact: 刚 sits before the verb: 刚来 'just arrived'. 刚才 'a moment ago' is a time word and can start a sentence. 刚好 means 'just right'. In writing 刚 also means 'firm': 刚强.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken particle
牙 (yá) is a close sound match for ya

example.fact: 呀 is 啊 after a syllable ending in a, e, i, o or u: 好呀 'great!', 快来呀. In 哎呀 'oh dear' it is yā. It adds warmth or urgency.

components.note: Simplified from 變; the modern shape is a shorthand

example.fact: 变 + adjective + 了 means 'become': 变冷了, 变好了. It also makes nouns: 变化 'change', 变成 'turn into', 变得 + degree: 他变得很高 'he has become tall'.

components.note: 木 (tree) — the whole tree
一 (line) — a mark at the bottom, pointing to the root

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
example.fact: 本 counts books and notebooks: 一本书. As 'root' it appears in 本来 'originally' and 根本 'fundamentally'. It also means 'this/our': 本人 'myself', 本月 'this month'. 日本 'Japan' means 'sun origin'.

components.note: 又 (hand) — in the simplified form this stands in for the old left part, so it is a shorthand
隹 (short-tailed bird) — the right part; the traditional account is a hand trying to grasp a bird

example.fact: 难 before a verb means 'hard to': 难吃 'bad-tasting', 难看 'ugly', 难过 'sad'. Read nàn it means 'disaster': 灾难 'calamity'. Its opposite is 容易 or 简单.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) — the lower part, a close sound match for měi

example.fact: 每 goes before a measure word or time: 每个人 'everyone', 每天 'every day', 每次 'each time'. 每个人 is usually followed by 都: 每个人都知道.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's share
分 (fēn) gives a close sound match for fèn

example.english: I'd like one portion of fried rice.
example.fact: 份 counts portions of food (一份饭), jobs (一份工作), newspapers (一份报纸) and documents. 身份 means 'identity', 月份 'month'.

components.note: 立 (stand) — standing
占 (zhàn) gives the sound exactly

example.fact: 站 means 'to stand' and a place where vehicles stop: 车站 'station', 火车站, 公交站 'bus stop', 网站 'website'. 站住！ is a command meaning 'Stop!'

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken exclamation
圭 (guī) is a loose sound hint for wā

example.fact: 哇 shows amazement, as in 'wow'. Doubled as 哇哇 it imitates a baby's crying. After u or ao the particle 啊 may become 哇: 好哇 (hǎo wa).

components.note: 夕 (evening) — dark, when you cannot be seen
口 (mouth) — you call out your name; the traditional account for 名

example.fact: 名字 is a full name: 名 'given name', 姓 'family name'. 名 also means 'fame' (出名 'famous') and ranks (第一名 'first place'). In formal counting it is a measure word for people: 三名学生.

components.note: 心 (heart) — the lower part, as in the older 總, which implies gathering one's thoughts

example.fact: 总是 means 'always' (habitual and a bit critical). 总共 is 'in total', 总统 'president', and 总会 means 'surely will eventually': 总会好的 'it will be fine in the end'. The simplified form is 總.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a lump of earth
夬 (guài) is a close sound match for kuài

example.english: I'd like a piece of cake.
example.fact: 块 counts lumps and pieces (一块肉, 一块蛋糕). In speech it also means 'yuan': 五块钱 'five yuan'. 一块儿 means 'together'. It is a casual alternative to written 元.

components.note: 卯 (mǎo) — the upper part, an old sound link to liú
田 (field) — the lower part, land where one stays

example.pinyin: Qǐng liúxià nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.fact: 留 is 'stay behind' or 'leave behind': 留下, 留言 'leave a message', 留学 'study abroad', 留意 'pay attention'. It can also mean 'keep': 留着 'save it'.

components.note: 冂 (frame) — a border all the way around, matching the sense 'circle, around'
土 (earth) — land inside the border
口 (box) — a small plot within, as in a divided field

example.fact: 周 is a written, modern way to say 'week': 周一 'Monday', 周末 'weekend', 下周 'next week'. It also means 'around': 周围 'surroundings'. It is a very common surname Zhōu as well.

components.note: 父 (father) — the meaning part
巴 (bā) is a close sound match for bà

example.fact: 爸 is usually doubled as 爸爸 in speech. The formal word is 父亲. Like 妈妈, 爸爸 resembles baby words for parents in many languages, because the sounds ba and ma are among babies' first.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people
两 (liǎng) gives a close sound match for liǎ

example.english: The two of us are good friends.
example.fact: 俩 comes after a pronoun to mean 'both of': 咱俩, 你们俩, 他们俩. It already includes the number two, so it takes no measure word. It is colloquial, with a contracted 两个. Read liǎng it means 'trick', as in 伎俩.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person stopping
亭 (tíng) gives the sound exactly

example.english: The car is parked at the door.
example.fact: 停 means 'stop' and 'park': 停车 'park a car', 停电 'power cut', 暂停 'pause'. The thing stops moving, which is different from 站, where someone stands. 别停！ means 'Don't stop!'

components.note: The origin is debated; learn it as a unit of 口 over 力

example.pinyin: Zhè shì lìng yí jiàn shì.
example.fact: 另 is 'another' or 'separately': 另一个 'another one', 另外 'in addition'. It is more formal than 别的 or 其他. Don't confuse 另 (lìng) with 别 (bié), which contains it.

components.note: A picture of the heart

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xīn tiào de hěn kuài.
example.fact: In Chinese thinking and feeling live in the heart: 开心 'happy', 小心 'careful', 担心 'worry', 放心 'relax'. Characters about thought and emotion carry 心 or 忄, such as 想 and 快.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — flowers are plants
化 (huà) is a close sound match for huā

example.pinyin: Tā sòng wǒ yì duǒ huā.
example.fact: 花 means 'flower' (measure word 朵) and also 'to spend': 花钱 'spend money', 花时间 'spend time'. It also means 'fancy, patterned': 花衣服 'patterned clothes'.
